The calm we had cultivated inside the estate was violently shattered on a rainy Thursday morning three weeks later.

I was at my corporate headquarters downtown, reviewing the final restructuring plans with Harrison, my attorney, when my phone buzzed aggressively against the glass conference table. It was Marcus, calling directly from the security command center at the estate.

"Mr. Sterling," Marcus’s voice came through the speakerphone, urgent and clipped. "We have a situation at the gates."

"What kind of situation?" I asked, frowning as Harrison paused his presentation.

"It’s your uncle's legal team, accompanied by two bailiffs and a local magistrate," Marcus explained grimly. "They’ve obtained a restraining order and an emergency asset-freeze injunction based on a newly filed countersuit. They're demanding immediate access to the main residence to inventory personal property and corporate records stored on-site."

I stood up immediately, knocking my chair back. "They're out on bail pending trial. They have no legal authority to seize residential assets based on civil countersuits filed after criminal indictments."

"They brought forged appellate paperwork, sir," Marcus said. "And more importantly... Mr. Sterling, Miss Clara is currently at the estate alone, overseeing the quarterly inventory audit. They forced their way past the outer gates before my men could block them."

A cold spike of adrenaline pierced my chest. Clara.

"Lock down the panic room in the master suite, Marcus. Get Clara inside immediately. Do not let those bastards touch her," I commanded, grabbing my overcoat from the back of my chair. "I'm heading home right now. If anyone crosses the threshold of my house before I get there, use whatever force is necessary."

I hung up before Marcus could reply, bolting out of the boardroom and sprinting toward the private elevators. Harrison called out something behind me, but I didn't care. My uncle was desperate, cornered like a rat, and he was lashing out at the only thing that mattered to me now.

The drive back to the estate felt agonizingly slow. Rain lashed against the windshield of my car as I pushed the engine past its limits, cutting through traffic with reckless abandon.

When I finally tore through the wrought-iron gates of the estate, the scene was chaotic. Two black sheriff's cruisers were parked across the circular driveway, their emergency lights flashing red and blue against the gray facade of the mansion. Standing on the grand front steps were two private investigators hired by Martin’s defense team, arguing aggressively with Marcus and three of my security guards.

I slammed my car door shut, ignoring the pouring rain as I marched up the steps like an approaching storm.

"What the hell do you think you're doing?" my voice boomed across the courtyard, cutting through the sound of the howling wind.

The lead investigator turned around, sneering. "Mr. Sterling. We have a court-ordered warrant to—"

"You have a piece of fraudulent paper signed by a corrupt judge who is currently under federal investigation," I snarled, stepping into his personal space, towering over him with cold, murderous fury in my eyes. "If you don't off this property in the next thirty seconds, I will personally ensure your private licenses are revoked permanently and you spend the rest of your lives defending yourselves in a federal penitentiary."

The investigator paled under my glare, reading the absolute lack of bluff in my expression. He muttered something to the bailiffs, and slowly, reluctantly, they began backing down the steps toward their vehicles.

"Marcus," I barked without looking back. "Where is Clara?"

"Inside, sir," Marcus replied, his jaw tight. "She locked herself in the master suite corridor as soon as they breached the door. They haven't reached her yet."
